English: Hermits Hut
A simple hut of wood and thatch, built for the first spiritual pioneers seeking solitude and prayer at the edge of the wilderness.
Simple Dormitory
Rough, communal quarters built from timber, providing shelter for a handful of monks dedicated to the monastic life.
Monastic Cell
Small, private cells built from stone and wood, offering solitude for monks to pray and study in greater comfort than before.
Communal Refectory
A timber and plaster dining hall where monks gather for shared meals, strengthening both body and spirit.
Scriptorium Annex
A modest extension for copying manuscripts and storing religious texts, fostering the spread of knowledge.
Enclosed Cloister
A stone quadrangle enclosing a peaceful courtyard, providing security and tranquility for the monastic community.
Abbots Quarters
Stately residential chambers for the abbot and visiting dignitaries, symbolizing the monasterys growing influence.
Expanded Dormitories
Substantial, stone-built living quarters for a large monastic population, reflecting the monasterys prosperity.
Grand Refectory
A vast, vaulted hall for communal feasts and gatherings, serving guests and the monastic order with grace and abundance.
Monastic Palace
A grand, palatial complex with ornate chapels, libraries, and gardens, standing as a beacon of faith, wealth, and learning across the land.
